sentences.quote:
Carlo Messina (Rome, 1962).
Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Intesa Sanpaolo since 29 September 2013.
sentences.text: Carlo Messina, born in Rome in 1962, has been Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Intesa Sanpaolo since 29 September 2013.

sentences.quote: A graduate of Economics and Business from Luiss University of Rome, he began his career at Banca Nazionale del Lavoro, where he held the position of Manager in charge of the Corporate Finance - Primary Markets and Corporate Finance Department. While developing his professional career, he carried out intense academic activities as Professor of Economics of Financial Intermediaries at the Business Administration Master of the Luiss School of Management and as Professor of Corporate Finance at the Department of Economics and Business of the University of Ancona.
sentences.text: A graduate in Economics and Business from Luiss University in Rome, he began his career at Banca Nazionale del Lavoro, where he was manager in charge of the Corporate Finance and Primary Markets department, and he also taught economics of financial intermediaries at the Luiss School of Management and corporate finance at the University of Ancona.

sentences.quote: In 1992, he joined Bonifiche Siele Finanziaria (Parent Company of the Banca Nazionale dell'Agricoltura banking group), where he held the position of Manager in charge of the Planning and Strategic Control Department. From 1996, he was Manager in charge of Planning at Banco Ambrosiano Veneto and, in 2002, he became the Head of the Planning and Control Head Office Department at Banca Intesa.
sentences.text: He joined Bonifiche Siele Finanziaria in 1992 as head of planning and strategic control, moved to Banco Ambrosiano Veneto in 1996 and in 2002 became head of the Planning and Control Head Office Department at Banca Intesa.

mgmt_bio.text: Carlo Messina, born in Rome in 1962, has been Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Intesa Sanpaolo since 29 September 2013. A graduate in Economics and Business from Luiss University in Rome, he began his career at Banca Nazionale del Lavoro, where he was manager in charge of the Corporate Finance and Primary Markets department, and he also taught economics of financial intermediaries at the Luiss School of Management and corporate finance at the University of Ancona. He joined Bonifiche Siele Finanziaria in 1992 as head of planning and strategic control, moved to Banco Ambrosiano Veneto in 1996 and in 2002 became head of the Planning and Control Head Office Department at Banca Intesa.

sentences.quote: SOLID SUSTAINABLE PROFITABILITY, WITH A 2025 NET INCOME OF EUR 9.3 BILLION (+7.6% VS 2024)
sentences.text: Under CEO Carlo Messina, Intesa Sanpaolo posted record 2025 net income of 9.3 billion euros, up 8% on 2024, with a return on equity of 18% and a cost-to-income ratio at an all-time low.

Execution continued in 2026: first-half profit of 5.6 billion euros prompted an increase in full-year guidance to above 10 billion euros, alongside planned shareholder returns of 9.4 billion euros via dividends and buybacks.

citations.title: Intesa Sanpaolo presents its 2026-2029 Business Plan: scaling a proven model with sustainable profitability and strong capital returns

sentences.quote: The Plan targets a sustainable ROE >20%
sentences.text: Intesa Sanpaolo's 2026-2029 Business Plan targets a sustainable ROE above 20% and roughly 50 billion euros of capital returned to shareholders over 2025-2029, with a 75% cash dividend payout plus buybacks of about 20%.
Wealth management and protection is the main growth engine, with record first-half 2026 commissions and insurance income, commissions up 5% and assets under management gross inflows up 7%.
First-half 2026 net income was a record 5.6 billion euros, up 6%, with 20% ROE and a cost-income ratio of 35.9%, and 2026 guidance was upgraded to more than 10 billion euros.

sentences.quote: the CET1 ratio will remain above 12.5%. Cost of risk is expected to remain in the range of 25-30 bp.
sentences.text: Capital stays rock-solid with a CET1 ratio above 12.5% and cost of risk guided at 25-30 basis points, alongside a zero-NPL profile.
The Monte dei Paschi di Siena transaction is expected to add further growth and value creation.
